signature: Iohann / Wilhelm / Haas / in Nurnberg; master’s mark, leaping hare
literature: Sachs 1922: col. 229; Lane 1982: 183-84, Herbert 2004; Wittenbrink 2005; Kempkes 2008
remarks: Since 1945 only 3 parts remain: garland, bell, and part of upper bell section. Museum files describe the instrument as part of an alto, though some earlier writers describe is as a tenor. Ascribing the instrument to Johann Wilhelm Haas is problematic, since the only known member of that distinguished family of brass-instrument makers was born in 1649. Detailed metal analysis in Kempkes 2008.
